expectations.text: Recommends that at least one of the two people sits off the floor, in no room, watching the outgoing feed as a remote attendee receives it
expectations.evidence: "Volunteer A is the event-wide watcher. They sit in no room and watch all three outgoing feeds."

expectations.text: States that a person standing beside the stage is the last to notice the stream has died
expectations.evidence: "An advocate beside a stage is the last person to notice the stream died."

expectations.text: States that the off-floor watcher costs less than an in-room advocate and catches feed failures better
expectations.evidence: The catching-failures half is covered, but no cost comparison is made.

expectations.text: Identifies service inside a session - relaying a question, acknowledging remote, telling the speaker remote is there - as the only axis on which the in-room advocate beats the off-floor watcher
expectations.evidence: Not framed this way.

expectations.text: Notes that one watcher covers however many rooms exist while advocates scale with the number of streamed rooms
expectations.evidence: "A fixed pair of advocates guards two rooms' Q&A. The watcher guards all three rooms' attention."

expectations.text: Notes that an advocate needs a session-by-session briefing on the programme while a watcher needs only the output
expectations.evidence: Not stated.

expectations.text: States that nobody standing in one room can see another room's output, given three rooms carry feeds
expectations.evidence: Says "It leaves nobody watching the output" but never states that someone in one room cannot see another room's feed.

expectations.text: Does not invent a ratio of remote-side staff to remote attendees
